title.zh: 卷八十二 列傳第三十二: 許敬宗 李義府
title.en: Volume 82 Biographies 32: Xu Jingzong, Li Yifu
title.raw: 卷八十二 列傳第三十二: 許敬宗 李義府 Volume 82 Biographies 32: Xu Jingzong, Li Yifu

sentences.zh: 許敬宗

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong

sentences.zh: 許敬宗，杭州新城人，隋禮部侍郎善心子也。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong was a man of Xincheng in Hangzhou, the son of Shanxin, Vice Minister of Rites of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong, a native of Xincheng in Hangzhou, was the son of Shanxin, Vice Minister of Rites under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 其先自高陽南渡，世仕江左。

translations.literal: His ancestors had crossed south from Gaoyang and for generations held office south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had migrated south from Gaoyang and for generations served in office in the Jiangzuo region.

sentences.zh: 敬宗幼善屬文，舉秀才，授淮陽郡司法書佐，俄直謁者台，奏通事舍人事。

translations.literal: Jingzong from youth was skilled at literary composition; he passed the xiucai examination and was appointed Judicial Assistant of Huaiyang Commandery. Soon he served at the Office of Imperial Reception and submitted matters as Tongshi Sheren.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong showed literary talent from an early age. After passing the xiucai examination he was made Judicial Assistant of Huaiyang Commandery, and soon afterward served at the Office of Imperial Reception, handling matters as a Tongshi Sheren.

sentences.zh: 江都之難，善心為宇文化及所害。

translations.literal: At the catastrophe of Jiangdu, Shanxin was killed by Yuwen Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: During the upheaval at Jiangdu, Shanxin was killed by Yuwen Huaji.

sentences.zh: 敬宗流轉，投於李密，密以為元帥府記室，與魏徵同為管記。

translations.literal: Jingzong wandered in exile and joined Li Mi, who made him Recorder of the Marshal's Headquarters; he and Wei Zheng both served as administrative clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong wandered in exile and attached himself to Li Mi, who appointed him Recorder of the Marshal's Headquarters. He and Wei Zheng both served as administrative recorders.

sentences.zh: 武德初，赤牒擬漣州別駕。

translations.literal: Early in the Wude era, a red document nominated him for Vice Prefect of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign, a red nomination slip proposed him for Vice Prefect of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其名，召補秦府學士。

translations.literal: When the Taizong Emperor heard his name, he summoned him to fill a post as Academician of the Prince of Qin's household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong heard of him, he summoned Jingzong to serve as an academician in the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年，累除著作郎，兼修國史，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Compiler, concurrently edited the National History, and was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In 634 he was promoted in succession to Compiler, concurrently edited the National History, and was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 十年，文德皇后崩，百官縗絰。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Wende Empress died, and all officials wore hemp mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: In 636, when Empress Wende died, all officials wore hemp mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 率更令歐陽詢狀貌醜異，眾或指之，敬宗見而大笑，為御史所劾，左授洪州都督府司馬。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Workshops Ouyang Xun had an ugly and strange appearance; the crowd sometimes pointed at him. Jingzong saw this and laughed aloud. He was impeached by the censorate and demoted to Military Assistant of the Hongzhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xun, Director of the Imperial Workshops, had a grotesque appearance, and people in the crowd would point at him. Jingzong saw this and burst out laughing. The censors impeached him, and he was demoted to Military Assistant under the Hongzhou Area Command.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中，兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Attendant and concurrently edited the National History.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Attendant and again served as an editor of the National History.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以修《武德》、《貞觀實錄》成，封高陽縣男，賜物八百段，權檢校黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because the compilation of the Veritable Records of Wude and Zhenguan was completed, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyang, granted eight hundred lengths of goods, and given acting appointment as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In 643, for completing the Veritable Records of the Wude and Zhenguan reigns, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyang, rewarded with eight hundred lengths of goods, and given acting appointment as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 高宗在春宮，遷太子右庶子。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was in the Eastern Palace, Jingzong was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozong was still crown prince, Jingzong was appointed Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 十九年，太宗親伐高麗，皇太子定州監國，敬宗與高士廉等共知機要。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Taizong Emperor personally campaigned against Goguryeo; the crown prince supervised the state at Dingzhou, and Jingzong together with Gao Shilian and others jointly handled confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 645, when Emperor Taizong campaigned in person against Goguryeo, the crown prince remained at Dingzhou to supervise the realm. Jingzong, together with Gao Shilian and others, jointly handled state secrets.

sentences.zh: 中書令岑文本卒於行所，令敬宗以本官檢校中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of the Secretariat Cen Wenti died on campaign, and Jingzong was ordered to act as Vice Director of the Secretariat while retaining his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Cen Wenti died on campaign, and Jingzong was ordered to serve as acting Vice Director of the Secretariat while keeping his original post.

sentences.zh: 太宗大破遼賊於駐蹕山，敬宗立於馬前受旨草詔書，詞彩甚麗，深見嗟賞。

translations.literal: The Taizong Emperor greatly defeated the Liao bandits at Mount Zhubi. Jingzong stood before his horse, received orders, and drafted an edict; the diction was very beautiful and he was deeply admired.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Zhubi the emperor won a great victory over the Liao forces. Jingzong stood before his horse, received his instructions, and drafted an edict on the spot. The prose was splendid, and the emperor greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 先是，庶人承乾廢黜，宮僚多被除削，久未收敘。

translations.literal: Earlier, the commoner Chengqian had been deposed; many palace officials had been dismissed and stripped of rank, and for a long time had not been restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the deposed former crown prince Chengqian had been cast aside, many of his palace staff had been dismissed and stripped of rank, and for a long time had not been restored to office.

sentences.zh: 敬宗上表曰：「臣聞先王慎罰，務在於恤刑，往哲寬仁，義在於宥過。

translations.literal: Jingzong submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the ancient kings were cautious in punishment and strove to show compassion in penal matters; the sages of old were generous and humane, and their principle lay in pardoning faults.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that the ancient kings were cautious in imposing punishments and strove to temper justice with mercy, while the sages of old were generous and humane and held that faults should be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 聖人之道，莫尚於茲。

translations.literal: In the way of the sage, nothing is more honored than this.
translations.idiomatic: Among the principles of the sages, none ranks higher than this.

sentences.zh: 竊見廢官，五品以上，除名棄斥，頗歷歲時。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that dismissed officials of the fifth rank and above, whose names were struck and who were cast out, have already passed through many years.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that dismissed officials of the fifth rank and above, whose names were struck from the rolls and who were cast out, have already endured many years in exile.

sentences.zh: 但庶人疇昔之年，身處不疑之地，苞藏悖逆，陰結宰臣，所預奸謀，多連宗戚。

translations.literal: Yet in years past the commoner, while occupying a position free from suspicion, harbored rebellion, secretly joined with chief ministers, and in the treacherous plots in which he took part many were linked through kin ties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in years past the deposed prince, though occupying a position that should have been above suspicion, harbored rebellion, secretly conspired with chief ministers, and in the plots in which he took part many of his kinsmen were implicated.

sentences.zh: 禍生慮表，非可防萌，宮內官僚，迥無關預。

translations.literal: Disaster arose beyond what could be foreseen and could not be prevented at its first sprouting; the palace officials within had no connection with it at all.
translations.idiomatic: The disaster arose beyond what could have been foreseen and could not have been stopped at the outset; the palace officials had no part in it whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 今乃投鼠及器，孰謂無冤？

translations.literal: Now in casting a rat one strikes the vessel as well—who would say there is no injustice?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now, in striking at the rat, the vessel is damaged as well—who can say there is no injustice in this?

sentences.zh: 焚山毀玉，稍同遷怒。

translations.literal: Burning the mountain and destroying the jade is somewhat like venting anger on the wrong target.
translations.idiomatic: To burn the mountain and destroy the jade is much like venting one's anger on the innocent.

sentences.zh: 伏尋先典，例有可原。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully examines the ancient statutes: precedent allows forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Upon examining the ancient statutes, I find that precedent allows for pardon.

sentences.zh: 昔吳國陪臣，則爰絲不坐於劉濞；

translations.literal: In former times, among the attendant ministers of Wu, Yuan Si was not punished for Liu Pi's crime;
translations.idiomatic: In former times, among the attendant ministers of Wu, Yuan Si was not punished for the crime of Liu Pi;

sentences.zh: 昌邑中尉，則王吉免緣於海昏。

translations.literal: the Commandant of Changyi, Wang Ji, was exempted from implication in the case of the Marquis of Haihun.
translations.idiomatic: and Wang Ji, Commandant of Changyi, was exempted from implication in the case of the Marquis of Haihun.

sentences.zh: 譬諸欒布，乃策名於彭越；

translations.literal: Compare Luan Bu, who made his name in the service of Peng Yue;
translations.idiomatic: Compare Luan Bu, who made his name while serving Peng Yue;

sentences.zh: 比乎田叔，亦委質於張敖。

translations.literal: or Tian Shu, who likewise pledged himself to Zhang Ao.
translations.idiomatic: or Tian Shu, who likewise pledged his service to Zhang Ao.

sentences.zh: 主以凶逆，陷其誅夷；

translations.literal: Their lords, because of treason and rebellion, fell into execution and extermination;
translations.idiomatic: Their lords, because of treason and rebellion, were executed and destroyed;

sentences.zh: 臣以賢良，荷彼收擢。

translations.literal: yet the ministers, because of their worth and goodness, were favored with recruitment and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: yet these ministers, because of their worth and integrity, were taken into service and promoted.

sentences.zh: 歷觀往代，此類尤多。

translations.literal: Surveying past ages, cases of this kind are especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back through the ages, such cases are especially numerous.

sentences.zh: 近者有隋，又遵斯義。

translations.literal: In recent times the Sui likewise followed this principle.
translations.idiomatic: Even in recent times the Sui followed this same principle.

sentences.zh: 楊勇之廢，罪止加於佞人，李綱之徒，皆不預於刑網。

translations.literal: When Yang Yong was deposed, guilt was limited to the flatterers; men such as Li Gang were none of them caught in the penal net.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yong was deposed, punishment fell only on the flatterers; men such as Li Gang were not caught in the net of the law.

sentences.zh: 古今裁其折衷，史籍稱為美談。

translations.literal: Ancient and modern judged this the balanced mean, and the historical records praise it as a fine example.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and modern alike have judged this the balanced course, and the histories praise it as a fine example.

sentences.zh: 而今張玄素、令狐德棻、趙弘智、裴宣機、蕭鈞等，並砥節勵操，有雅望於當朝；

translations.literal: Yet now Zhang Xuansu, Linghu Defen, Zhao Hongzhi, Pei Xuanji, Xiao Jun, and others all sharpen their integrity and strengthen their conduct, and enjoy refined repute in the present court;
translations.idiomatic: Yet now Zhang Xuansu, Linghu Defen, Zhao Hongzhi, Pei Xuanji, Xiao Jun, and others all hold fast to integrity and enjoy refined repute at court;

sentences.zh: 經明行修，播令名於天下。

translations.literal: they are versed in the classics and cultivated in conduct, and spread a fine name throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: they are versed in the classics and cultivated in conduct, and their good names are known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 或以直言而遭箠撲，或以忤意而見猜嫌，一概雷同，並罹天憲，恐於王道，傷在未弘。」

translations.literal: Some because of blunt speech suffered beating, others because of displeasing the ruler met with suspicion—treated all alike, they alike fell under Heaven's law. This may harm the kingly way, for the injury lies in its lack of breadth."
translations.idiomatic: Some because of blunt speech were beaten, others because they displeased the throne met with suspicion—treated all alike, they alike fell under imperial punishment. This may harm the kingly way, for the injury lies in its lack of magnanimity."

sentences.zh: 由是玄素等稍得敘用。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuansu and the others gradually obtained restoration to office.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xuansu and the others were gradually restored to office.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was given the additional title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In 647 he was given the additional title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，代於志寧為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Jingzong replaced Yu Zhining as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Jingzong replaced Yu Zhining as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嫁女與蠻酋馮盎之子，多納金寶，為有司所劾，左授鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingzong gave his daughter in marriage to the son of the barbarian chieftain Feng Ang and accepted much gold and treasure. He was impeached by the responsible officials and demoted to Prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong gave his daughter in marriage to the son of the tribal chieftain Feng Ang and accepted large gifts of gold and treasure. The authorities impeached him, and he was demoted to Prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，入為衛尉卿，加弘文館學士，兼修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui he entered the capital as Commandant of the Guards, was made Academician of the Hongwen Hall, and concurrently edited the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In 652 he returned to the capital as Commandant of the Guards, was made an academician of the Hongwen Hall, and again edited the National History.

sentences.zh: 六年，復拜禮部尚書，高宗將廢皇后王氏而立武昭儀，敬宗特贊成其計。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again appointed Minister of Rites. When Gaozong was about to depose Empress Wang and establish Lady Wu as consort, Jingzong especially supported the plan.
translations.idiomatic: In 655 he was again appointed Minister of Rites. When Gaozong planned to depose Empress Wang and elevate Lady Wu, Jingzong strongly supported the scheme.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌、褚遂良、韓瑗等並直言忤旨，敬宗與李義府潛加誣構，並流死於嶺外。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and others all spoke bluntly against the imperial will. Jingzong and Li Yifu secretly added false charges against them, and they were all exiled and died beyond the mountain ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and others all spoke bluntly against the emperor's will. Jingzong and Li Yifu secretly fabricated charges against them, and they were all exiled and died in the far south.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，加太子賓客，尋冊拜侍中，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he was made Guest of the Crown Prince; soon he was appointed Palace Attendant and supervised the editing of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In 656 he was made Guest of the Crown Prince, and soon afterward was appointed Palace Attendant and put in charge of editing the National History.

sentences.zh: 三年，進封郡公，尋贈其父善心為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced to enfeoffment as Duke of a commandery, and soon his father Shanxin was posthumously granted the title Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 658 he was advanced to Duke of a commandery, and soon his father Shanxin was posthumously granted the title Prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗因於古長安城遊覽，問侍臣曰：「朕觀故城舊基，宮室似與百姓雜居，自秦、漢已來，幾代都此？」

translations.literal: Gaozong, while touring the old city of Chang'an, asked his attendant ministers: "When I look at the old foundations of the former city, the palaces seem to have been mixed in with the common people. Since the Qin and Han, how many dynasties have made this their capital?"
translations.idiomatic: While touring the old city of Chang'an, Gaozong asked his ministers, "When I look at the old foundations here, the palaces seem to have been mixed in with the common people. Since the Qin and Han, how many dynasties have made this their capital?"

sentences.zh: 敬宗對曰：「秦都咸陽，郭邑連跨渭水，故云『渭水貫都，以象天河。』

translations.literal: Jingzong replied: "The Qin made their capital at Xianyang; the outer city stretched across the Wei River, hence the saying, 'The Wei River runs through the capital, symbolizing the River of Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong replied, "The Qin made their capital at Xianyang, and the outer city stretched across the Wei River. Hence the saying, 'The Wei River runs through the capital, symbolizing the River of Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 至漢惠帝始築此城，其後苻堅、姚萇、後周並都之。」

translations.literal: It was only under Emperor Hui of Han that this city was first built; afterward Fu Jian, Yao Chang, and the Later Zhou all made it their capital."
translations.idiomatic: It was only under Emperor Hui of Han that this city was first built. Afterward Fu Jian, Yao Chang, and the Later Zhou all made it their capital."

sentences.zh: 帝又問：「昆明池是漢武帝何年中開鑿？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked again: "In which year of Emperor Wu of Han was Kunming Pool excavated?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, "In which year of Emperor Wu of Han was Kunming Pool excavated?"

sentences.zh: 敬宗對曰：「武帝遣使通西南夷，而為昆明滇池所閉，欲伐昆明國，故因鎬之舊澤，以穿此池，用習水戰，元狩三年事也。」

translations.literal: Jingzong replied: "Emperor Wu sent envoys to open relations with the southwestern barbarians, but they were blocked by the Kunming people at Dian Lake. Wishing to attack the state of Kunming, he therefore used the old marshlands of Hao to cut this pool and practice naval warfare. This was in the third year of Yuanshuo."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong replied, "Emperor Wu sent envoys to open relations with the southwestern tribes, but they were blocked at Dian Lake by the Kunming people. Wishing to attack the state of Kunming, he used the old marshlands of the Hao region to excavate this pool for naval training. This took place in 120 BCE, the third year of Yuanshuo."

sentences.zh: 帝因令敬宗與弘文館學士具檢秦、漢已來歷代宮室處所以奏。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon ordered Jingzong and the academicians of the Hongwen Hall fully to examine and report on the sites of palaces of successive dynasties since the Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Jingzong and the Hongwen Hall academicians to research fully the sites of palaces of successive dynasties since the Qin and Han and submit a report.

sentences.zh: 其年，代李義府為中書令，任遇之重，當朝莫比。

translations.literal: That year he replaced Li Yifu as Chief Minister of the Secretariat; the weight of his appointment and favor was unmatched in the court of his day.
translations.idiomatic: That year he replaced Li Yifu as Chief Minister of the Secretariat, and the favor shown him was unmatched at court.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，從新令改為右相，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, under the new statutes he was changed to Right Chancellor and given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In 662, under the new statutes, he was redesignated Right Chancellor and given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 三年，冊拜太子少師、同東西台三品，並依舊監修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed by edict Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and Associate of the Third Rank of the Eastern and Western Offices, and as before supervised the editing of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In 663 he was formally appointed Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and Associate of the Third Rank of the Eastern and Western Offices, and as before supervised the editing of the National History.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，以敬宗年老，不能行步，特令與司空李勣，每朝日各乘小馬入禁門至內省。

translations.literal: Early in the Qianfeng era, because Jingzong was old and could not walk, he was specially ordered together with Sikong Li Ji that on each court day they should each ride a small horse through the forbidden gate to the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianfeng era, because Jingzong was elderly and could no longer walk, he and Sikong Li Ji were specially permitted each court day to ride small horses through the forbidden gate to the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 敬宗自掌知國史，記事阿曲。

translations.literal: Jingzong personally controlled the National History and in recording events flattered and bent the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jingzong took charge of the National History, he recorded events in a flattering and distorted manner.

sentences.zh: 初，虞世基與敬宗父善心同為宇文化及所害，封德彝時為內史舍人，備見其事，因謂人曰：「世基被誅，世南匍匐而請代；

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu Shiji and Jingzong's father Shanxin were both killed by Yuwen Huaji. Feng Deyi was then Secretariat Drafter and witnessed the whole affair in detail. He therefore said to others: "When Shiji was executed, Shinan crawled prostrate to beg to take his place;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yu Shiji and Jingzong's father Shanxin were both killed by Yuwen Huaji. Feng Deyi, then a Secretariat drafter, witnessed the whole affair and said to others, "When Shiji was executed, Shinan crawled prostrate to beg to die in his place;

sentences.zh: 善心之死，敬宗舞蹈以求生。」

translations.literal: when Shanxin died, Jingzong danced and capered to beg for his life."
translations.idiomatic: when Shanxin was killed, Jingzong danced and capered to beg for his life."

sentences.zh: 人以為口實，敬宗深銜之，及為德彝立傳，盛加其罪惡。

translations.literal: People took this as a byword, and Jingzong deeply resented it. When he wrote a biography for Deyi, he greatly exaggerated his crimes and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: People repeated this as a byword, and Jingzong deeply resented it. When he wrote Deyi's biography, he greatly exaggerated his crimes and wickedness.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嫁女與左監門大將軍錢九隴，本皇家隸人，敬宗貪財與婚，乃為九隴曲敘門閥，妄加功績，並升與劉文靜、長孫順德同卷。

translations.literal: Jingzong gave his daughter in marriage to Qian Jiulong, General of the Left Gate Guards, who was originally a bondservant of the imperial house. Jingzong, greedy for wealth, entered the marriage alliance and therefore for Jiulong bent the account of his lineage, falsely added achievements, and elevated him to the same scroll as Liu Wenjing and Zhangsun Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong gave his daughter in marriage to Qian Jiulong, General of the Left Gate Guards, who had originally been an imperial bondservant. Greedy for money, Jingzong entered the marriage and then falsified Jiulong's lineage, invented achievements for him, and placed his biography in the same scroll as those of Liu Wenjing and Zhangsun Shunde.

sentences.zh: 敬宗為子娶尉遲寶琳孫女為妻，多得賂遺，及作寶琳父敬德傳，悉為隱諸過咎。

translations.literal: Jingzong had his son take the granddaughter of Yuchi Baolin as wife and received many bribes. When he wrote the biography of Baolin's father Jingde, he concealed all faults and errors.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong had his son marry the granddaughter of Yuchi Baolin and accepted many bribes from the family. When he wrote the biography of Baolin's father Jingde, he concealed all their faults.

sentences.zh: 太宗作《威鳳賦》以賜長孫無忌，敬宗改雲賜敬德。

translations.literal: The Taizong Emperor composed the "Rhapsody on the Majestic Phoenix" to bestow on Zhangsun Wuji, but Jingzong altered the record to say it was bestowed on Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had composed the "Rhapsody on the Majestic Phoenix" to bestow on Zhangsun Wuji, but Jingzong altered the record to say it had been bestowed on Jingde.

sentences.zh: 白州人龐孝泰，蠻酋凡品，率兵從征高麗，賊知其懦，襲破之。

translations.literal: Pang Xiaotai of Baizhou, a barbarian chieftain of ordinary rank, led troops on the campaign against Goguryeo. The enemy knew he was cowardly and attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xiaotai of Baizhou, a tribal chieftain of ordinary rank, led troops on the campaign against Goguryeo. The enemy knew he was timid, attacked him, and routed his force.

sentences.zh: 敬宗又納其寶貨，稱孝泰頻破賊徒，斬獲數萬。

translations.literal: Jingzong again accepted his treasures and reported that Xiaotai repeatedly defeated the bandits and beheaded and captured tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong again accepted bribes from him and reported that Xiaotai had repeatedly defeated the enemy and killed or captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 漢將驍健者，唯蘇定方與龐孝泰耳，曹繼叔、劉伯英皆出其下。

translations.literal: Among the valiant Han generals, only Su Dingfang and Pang Xiaotai were such; Cao Jishu and Liu Boying were both beneath them.
translations.idiomatic: Among valiant Han generals, only Su Dingfang and Pang Xiaotai were his equals, while Cao Jishu and Liu Boying were beneath him.

sentences.zh: 虛美隱惡如此！

translations.literal: Thus did he praise falsely and conceal evil!
translations.idiomatic: Such was the extent of his false praise and concealment of wrongdoing!

sentences.zh: 初，高祖、太宗兩朝實錄，其敬播所修者，頗多詳直，敬宗又輒以己愛憎曲事刪改，論者尤之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Veritable Records of the Gaozu and Taizong reigns, the portions compiled by Xu Jingbo were in many places detailed and straightforward, but Jingzong again repeatedly deleted and altered events according to his own likes and dislikes, and critics especially blamed him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Veritable Records of the Gaozu and Taizong reigns, the portions compiled by Xu Jingbo were in many places detailed and straightforward, but Jingzong repeatedly revised events according to his own likes and dislikes, and critics especially condemned him for this.

sentences.zh: 然自貞觀已來，朝廷所修《五代史》及《晉書》、《東殿新書》、《西域圖志》、《文思博要》、《文館詞林》、《累璧》、《瑤山玉彩》《姓氏錄》、《新禮》，皆總知其事，前後賞賚，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Yet from the Zhenguan era onward, in such works as the History of the Five Dynasties, the Book of Jin, the New Book of the Eastern Hall, the Gazetteer of the Western Regions, the Comprehensive Digest of Literary Thought, the Forest of Literary Phrases of the Literary Hall, the Accumulated Jade, the Jade Splendor of Mount Yao, the Register of Surnames, and the New Rites—all compiled at court—he was in overall charge, and the rewards granted him before and after are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Zhenguan era onward, he was placed in overall charge of such court compilations as the History of the Five Dynasties, the Book of Jin, the New Book of the Eastern Hall, the Gazetteer of the Western Regions, the Comprehensive Digest of Literary Thought, the Forest of Literary Phrases of the Literary Hall, the Accumulated Jade, the Jade Splendor of Mount Yao, the Register of Surnames, and the New Rites, and the rewards he received before and after are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 敬宗好色無度。

translations.literal: Jingzong was licentious beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong was licentious beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 其長子昂頗有才藻，歷位太子舍人。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ang was quite gifted in literary talent and rose to the post of Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ang was quite gifted in letters and rose to the post of Attendant of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 母裴氏早卒。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Pei, died early.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Pei, had died early.

sentences.zh: 裴侍婢有姿色，敬宗嬖之，以為繼室，假姓虞氏。

translations.literal: A maidservant of the Pei household had beauty; Jingzong favored her, made her his successor wife, and gave her the false surname Lady Yu.
translations.idiomatic: A maidservant of the Pei household was beautiful, and Jingzong favored her, made her his successor wife, and gave her the false surname Yu.

sentences.zh: 昂素與通，烝之不絕，敬宗怒黜虞氏，加昂以不孝，奏請流於嶺外。

translations.literal: Ang had long been intimate with her and continued the affair without cease. Jingzong in anger dismissed Lady Yu, charged Ang with unfilial conduct, and memorialized requesting his exile beyond the mountain ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Ang had long been intimate with her and continued the affair without cease. Jingzong in anger dismissed Lady Yu, charged Ang with unfilial conduct, and memorialized requesting his exile to the far south.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，表乞昂還，除虔化令，尋卒。

translations.literal: During Xianqing he memorialized begging that Ang be returned, appointed him Magistrate of Qianhua, and soon Ang died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianqing era he memorialized asking that Ang be recalled, appointed him Magistrate of Qianhua, and Ang soon died.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，抗表乞骸骨，詔聽致仕，仍加特進，俸祿如舊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng he submitted a memorial begging to retire on account of old bones. An edict permitted him to leave office, and he was still given the special advancement rank; his salary remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 670 he submitted a memorial asking to retire on account of age. The emperor permitted him to leave office, granted him the special advancement rank, and kept his salary unchanged.

sentences.zh: 三年薨，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In 672 he died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 高宗為之舉哀，廢朝三日，詔文武百官就第赴哭，冊贈開府儀同三司、揚州大都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Gaozong mourned for him, suspended court for three days, and ordered civil and military officials to go to his residence to wail. By edict he was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Ribbon of the First Rank and Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, and he was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong mourned for him, suspended court for three days, and ordered civil and military officials to go to his residence to wail. He was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Ribbon of the First Rank and Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, and was buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 文集八十捲。

translations.literal: His collected writings were eighty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to eighty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 太常將定謚，博士袁思古議曰：「敬宗位以才升，歷居清級，然棄長子於荒徼，嫁少女於夷落。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices was about to fix his posthumous name. Academician Yuan Sigu proposed: "Jingzong rose in rank through talent and for a long time held a pure office, yet he abandoned his eldest son in the wild borderlands and gave his young daughter in marriage to a barbarian settlement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was about to fix his posthumous name, Academician Yuan Sigu proposed, "Jingzong rose through talent and long held a high office, yet he abandoned his eldest son in the wild borderlands and gave his young daughter in marriage to a barbarian settlement.

sentences.zh: 聞《詩》學《禮》，事絕於趨庭；

translations.literal: To hear the Odes and study the Rites—such things ended at the courtyard gate;
translations.idiomatic: To hear the Odes and study the Rites—such things ended at the courtyard gate;

sentences.zh: 納采問名，唯聞於黷貨。

translations.literal: in betrothal gifts and asking the name, one hears only of corrupt wealth.
translations.idiomatic: in betrothal gifts and asking the bride's name, one hears only of bribes.

sentences.zh: 白圭斯玷，有累清塵，易名之典，須憑實行。

translations.literal: The white jade has its stain and mars the clear dust; the canon of changing the name must rely on actual conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The white jade has its stain and mars his fair reputation; the canon of posthumous naming must rely on actual conduct.

sentences.zh: 按謚法『名與實爽曰繆』，請謚為『繆』。」

translations.literal: According to the canon of posthumous names, 'when name and reality diverge, it is called Miu,' and I request the posthumous name Miu."
translations.idiomatic: According to the canon of posthumous names, 'when name and reality diverge, the name is Miu,' and I request the posthumous name Miu."

sentences.zh: 敬宗孫、太子舍人彥伯不勝其恥，與思古大相忿競，又稱思古與許氏先有嫌隙，請改謚官。

translations.literal: Jingzong's grandson Yanbo, Attendant of the Crown Prince, could not bear the shame and quarreled fiercely with Sigu. He also claimed that Sigu had long borne a grudge against the Xu clan and requested that the posthumous-name officials be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong's grandson Yanbo, Attendant of the Crown Prince, could not bear the shame and quarreled fiercely with Sigu. He also claimed that Sigu had long borne a grudge against the Xu clan and requested that different officials be assigned to fix the posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 太常博士王福畤議曰：「謚者，飾終之稱也，得失一朝，榮辱千載。

translations.literal: Academician Wang Fuchou of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed: "A posthumous name is the title that adorns the end; gain and loss last but a morning, yet honor and shame endure a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Wang Fuchou of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed, "A posthumous name is the title that adorns a man's end; gain and loss last but a morning, yet honor and shame endure a thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 若使嫌隙是實，即合據法推繩；

translations.literal: If the grudge is real, then one should apply the law and pursue punishment;
translations.idiomatic: If the grudge is real, then the law should be applied and punishment pursued;

sentences.zh: 如其不虧直道，義不可奪，官不可侵。

translations.literal: if he has not failed the straight path, then righteousness cannot be taken away, nor may office be encroached upon.
translations.idiomatic: if he has not failed the straight path, then righteousness cannot be set aside, nor may his office be encroached upon.

sentences.zh: 二三其德，何以言禮？

translations.literal: To be of two or three minds in virtue—how can one speak of ritual?
translations.idiomatic: To be of two minds in virtue—how can one speak of ritual propriety?

sentences.zh: 福畤忝當官守，匪躬之故。

translations.literal: Fuchou, though unworthy, holds this official charge for the sake of not failing in one's person.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchou, though unworthy, holds this office and must not fail in his duty.

sentences.zh: 若順風阿意，背直從曲，更是甲令虛設，將謂禮院無人，何以激揚雅道，顧視同列！

translations.literal: If one follows the wind and flatters intent, turning one's back on the straight and following the crooked, this would make the statutes a dead letter and show the Court of Rites to have no men. How then could one inspire the refined way and face one's colleagues!
translations.idiomatic: If one follows the wind and flatters power, turning one's back on the straight and following the crooked, the statutes become a dead letter and the Court of Rites is shown to have no men of integrity. How then could one inspire the refined way and face one's colleagues!

sentences.zh: 請依思古謚議為定。」

translations.literal: I request that Sigu's posthumous-name proposal be adopted as final."
translations.idiomatic: I request that Sigu's posthumous-name proposal be adopted as final."

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書戴至德謂福畤曰：「高陽公任遇如此，何以定謚為『繆』？」

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Dai Zhide said to Fuchou: "The Duke of Gaoyang received such favor and appointment—how can his posthumous name be fixed as Miu?"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Dai Zhide said to Fuchou, "The Duke of Gaoyang received such favor and appointment—how can his posthumous name be fixed as Miu?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「昔晉司空何曾薨，太常博士秦秀謚為繆丑公。

translations.literal: He replied: "In former times, when He Zeng, Minister of Works of Jin, died, Academician Qin Xiu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices gave him the posthumous name Duke Miu Chou.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In former times, when He Zeng, Minister of Works of Jin, died, Academician Qin Xiu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices gave him the posthumous name Duke Miu Chou.

sentences.zh: 何曾既忠且孝，徒以日食萬錢，所以貶為繆丑。

translations.literal: He Zeng was both loyal and filial, yet solely because he spent ten thousand cash a day on food, he was therefore demoted to Miu Chou.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng was both loyal and filial, yet solely because he spent ten thousand cash a day on food, he was given the demeaning name Miu Chou.

sentences.zh: 況敬宗忠孝不逮於曾，飲食男女之累，有逾於何氏，而謚之為『繆』，無負於許氏矣。」

translations.literal: How much more does Jingzong fall short of Zeng in loyalty and filial piety, while the burdens of food, drink, and women exceed those of the He clan—yet to give him the posthumous name Miu does the Xu clan no injustice."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong falls far short of Zeng in loyalty and filial piety, while his indulgence in food, drink, and women exceeds even the He clan—yet to give him the posthumous name Miu does the Xu clan no injustice."

sentences.zh: 時有詔令尚書省五品已上重議，禮部尚書袁思敬議稱：「按謚法『既過能改曰恭』，請謚曰『恭』。」

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered officials of the fifth rank and above in the Ministry of State Affairs to deliberate again. Minister of Rites Yuan Sijing proposed: "According to the canon of posthumous names, 'having faults but able to reform is called Gong,' and I request the posthumous name Gong."
translations.idiomatic: At that time an edict ordered officials of the fifth rank and above in the Ministry of State Affairs to deliberate again. Minister of Rites Yuan Sijing proposed, "According to the canon of posthumous names, 'having faults but able to reform is called Gong,' and I request the posthumous name Gong."

sentences.zh: 詔從其議。

translations.literal: An edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed his proposal.

sentences.zh: 彥伯，昂之子，起家著作郎。

translations.literal: Yanbo was the son of Ang. He entered office as Editing Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo, the son of Ang, began his career as an Editing Clerk.

sentences.zh: 敬宗末年文筆，多令彥伯代作。

translations.literal: In Jingzong's final years, most of his literary compositions were ordered to be drafted by Yanbo in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In Xu Jingzong's last years, Yanbo was often asked to draft his compositions for him.

sentences.zh: 又納婢妾讒言，奏流於嶺表，後遇赦得還，除太子舍人。

translations.literal: He also took in a maidservant concubine whose slander led to a memorial exiling him to the Ling region. Later he encountered an amnesty and was allowed to return, and was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He also took in a maidservant concubine who spread slander against him; a memorial had him exiled to the far south. After an amnesty allowed his return, he was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 早卒，有集十捲。

translations.literal: He died young. He had a collected writings in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He died young, leaving a collected writings in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 李義府

translations.literal: Li Yifu
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu

sentences.zh: 李義府，瀛州饒陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Yifu was a man of Raoyang in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu was a native of Raoyang in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其祖為梓州射洪縣丞，因家於永泰。

translations.literal: His grandfather had served as assistant magistrate of Shehong County in Zizhou, and the family settled at Yongtai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had served as assistant magistrate of Shehong County in Zizhou, and the family thereafter made its home at Yongtai.

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年，劍南道巡察大使李大亮以義府善屬文，表薦之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan, Li Daliang, touring inspector of the Jiannan Circuit, because Yifu was skilled at literary composition, submitted a memorial recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenguan, Li Daliang, touring inspector of the Jiannan Circuit, recommended Yifu in a memorial, citing his skill at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 對策擢第，補門下省典儀。

translations.literal: In the palace examination he was placed in the top tier and was appointed Ceremonial Officer in the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He placed at the top of the palace examination and was appointed Ceremonial Officer in the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎劉洎、侍書御史馬周皆稱薦之，尋除監察御史。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Chancellery Liu Ji and Palace Secretariat Censor Ma Zhou both praised and recommended him, and soon thereafter he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Chancellery Liu Ji and Palace Secretariat Censor Ma Zhou both praised and recommended him, and he was soon appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 又敕義府以本官兼侍晉王。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Yifu to serve concurrently in his original post as attendant to Prince Jin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered Yifu to retain his original post while serving concurrently as attendant to Prince Jin.

sentences.zh: 及升春宮，除太子舍人，加崇賢館直學士，與太子司議郎來濟俱以文翰見知，時稱來、李。

translations.literal: When [the prince] ascended to the Eastern Palace, [Yifu] was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent and additionally Direct Academician of the Chongxian Hall. Together with Lai Ji, Reviewer of Memorials for the Heir Apparent, he was known for his literary talent; at the time they were called Lai and Li.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Yifu was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent and additionally Direct Academician of the Chongxian Hall. He and Lai Ji, Reviewer of Memorials for the Heir Apparent, were both known for their literary talent; at the time they were called Lai and Li.

sentences.zh: 義府嘗獻《承華箴》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: Yifu once presented the "Admonition on Upholding Splendor" (Chenghua Zhen); its text reads:
translations.idiomatic: Yifu once presented the Admonition on Upholding Splendor (Chenghua Zhen); its text reads:

sentences.zh: 邃初冥昧，元氣氤氳。

translations.literal: In the deep beginning, dark and obscure; primordial qi was thick and swirling.
translations.idiomatic: In the utter beginning all was dark and obscure, and primordial breath swirled in mist.

sentences.zh: 二儀始闡，三才既分。

translations.literal: The Two Powers first opened forth; the Three Potentials were then divided.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth first unfolded, and the three realms of Heaven, Earth, and Man were set apart.

sentences.zh: 司乾立宰，出《震》為君。

translations.literal: Heaven set forth its rule and established the lord; from the hexagram Zhen (Thunder) the ruler emerges.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven ordained governance and raised up the sovereign; from the hexagram Zhen the ruler emerges—as eldest son and heir.

sentences.zh: 化昭淳樸，道映典墳。

translations.literal: Transforming influence illuminates simplicity and purity; the Way mirrors the canonical texts.
translations.idiomatic: Civilizing influence reveals simplicity and purity; the Way is reflected in the canonical texts.

sentences.zh: 功成揖讓，事極華、勳。

translations.literal: When merit is complete, the throne is yielded in abdication; affairs reach their height with Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: When merit is complete, the throne is yielded in abdication; the model reaches its height with Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 肇興夏啟，降及姬文。

translations.literal: It began with Xia Qi and descended to King Wen of the Ji clan.
translations.idiomatic: It began with Qi of Xia and descended to King Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 咸資繼德，永樹高芬。

translations.literal: All rely on inheriting virtue and forever plant lofty fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: All rely on inheriting virtue and forever plant their lofty renown.

sentences.zh: 百代沿襲，千齡奉聖。

translations.literal: For a hundred generations the succession has been handed down; for a thousand ages the sage has been revered.
translations.idiomatic: For a hundred generations the succession has endured; for a thousand ages the sage has been revered.

sentences.zh: 粵若我後，丕承寶命。

translations.literal: Thus our sovereign, grandly inheriting the precious Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Thus our sovereign, grandly inheriting the precious Mandate of Heaven—

sentences.zh: 允穆三階，爰齊七政。

translations.literal: Has brought true harmony to the three ranks and aligned himself with the seven regulators.
translations.idiomatic: has brought true harmony to the three ranks and aligned himself with the seven regulators of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 時雍化洽，風移俗盛。

translations.literal: Universal harmony pervades; the wind shifts and customs flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Universal harmony pervades; customs shift and the age flourishes.

sentences.zh: 載崇國本，式延家慶。

translations.literal: He bears up the foundation of the state and extends the felicity of the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: He uplifts the foundation of the state and extends the fortune of the royal house.

sentences.zh: 《震》維標德，《離》警體正。

translations.literal: The hexagram Zhen marks virtue; the hexagram Li warns one to keep one's form correct.
translations.idiomatic: The hexagram Zhen marks the crown prince's virtue; the hexagram Li warns him to keep his conduct correct.

sentences.zh: 寄切宗祧，事隆監撫。

translations.literal: His charge touches the ancestral line; his affairs are elevated to supervision and nurture.
translations.idiomatic: His charge touches the ancestral line; his office is to oversee and nurture the realm.

sentences.zh: 思皇茂則，敬詢端輔。

translations.literal: Bear in mind the sovereign's abundant norms; respectfully seek counsel from upright ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Bear in mind the sovereign's abundant norms; respectfully seek counsel from upright ministers.

sentences.zh: 業光啟、誦，藝優干羽。

translations.literal: Let achievements shine like those of Qi and Song; let arts excel as in the Shield-and-Axe Dance.
translations.idiomatic: Let your achievements shine like those of Qi and Song; let your arts excel as in the Shield-and-Axe Dance.

sentences.zh: 九載崇儒，三朝問豎，歷選儲儀，遺文在斯。

translations.literal: Nine years honoring the ru tradition, thrice at court questioning the learned—regulations for the heir have been chosen through the ages, and the legacy texts remain here.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years honoring the Confucian tradition, thrice at court questioning the learned—regulations for the heir have been chosen through the ages, and the legacy texts remain with us.

sentences.zh: 望試登俎，高諭喬枝。

translations.literal: Look to trial upon the ritual altar; let lofty instruction reach the towering branch.
translations.idiomatic: Look to trial upon the ritual altar; let lofty instruction reach the towering branch.

sentences.zh: 俯容思順，非禮無施。

translations.literal: Bow in humility, think of compliance; let nothing unfitting be done.
translations.idiomatic: Bow in humility and think of compliance; let nothing unfitting be done.

sentences.zh: 前修盛業，來哲通規。

translations.literal: The great achievements of former worthies, the universal standards of sages to come.
translations.idiomatic: The great achievements of former worthies, the universal standards of sages to come—

sentences.zh: 飭躬是蹈，則叡問風馳；

translations.literal: If you discipline your person and follow their path, then sagely inquiry will come swift as the wind;
translations.idiomatic: if you discipline your person and follow their path, then sagely inquiry will come swift as the wind;

sentences.zh: 立志或爽，則玄猷日虧。

translations.literal: if your resolve should falter, then your deep designs will daily fall away.
translations.idiomatic: if your resolve should falter, then your deep designs will daily fall away.

sentences.zh: 無恃尊極，修途難測；

translations.literal: Do not trust in supreme rank—the upward path is hard to measure;
translations.idiomatic: Do not trust in supreme rank—the upward path is hard to measure;

sentences.zh: 無恃親賢，失德靡全。

translations.literal: do not trust in closeness to the virtuous—lose virtue and none is whole.
translations.idiomatic: do not trust in closeness to the virtuous—lose virtue and none of you is whole.

sentences.zh: 勿輕小善，積小而名自聞；

translations.literal: Do not slight small acts of goodness; gather them and your name will rise of itself;
translations.idiomatic: Do not slight small acts of goodness; gather them and your name will rise of itself;

sentences.zh: 勿輕微行，累微而身自正。

translations.literal: do not slight conduct; accumulate it and your person will be set right of itself.
translations.idiomatic: do not slight conduct; accumulate it and your person will be set right of itself.

sentences.zh: 佞諛有類，邪巧多方。

translations.literal: Flattery and sycophancy come in kinds; crooked cunning takes many forms.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery and sycophancy come in kinds; crooked cunning takes many forms.

sentences.zh: 其萌不絕，其害必彰。

translations.literal: If their sprouts are not cut off, their harm is sure to show.
translations.idiomatic: If their sprouts are not cut off, their harm is sure to show.

sentences.zh: 監言斯屏，儲業攸昌。

translations.literal: When such words are barred from the heir's ear, his charge will flourish.
translations.idiomatic: When such words are barred from the heir's ear, his charge will flourish.

sentences.zh: 竊惟令嗣，有殊前事。

translations.literal: I humbly consider our heir apparent: his case differs from those before.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider our heir apparent: his case differs from those before.

sentences.zh: 雖以貴以賢，而非長非次。

translations.literal: Though honored for rank and virtue, he is neither the eldest son nor next in order of birth.
translations.idiomatic: Though honored for rank and virtue, he is neither the eldest son nor next in order of birth.

sentences.zh: 皇明眷德，超倫作貳。

translations.literal: The imperial grace, cherishing his virtue, set him above his peers as second to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grace, cherishing his virtue, set him above his peers as heir to the throne.

sentences.zh: 匪懋聲華，莫酬恩異。

translations.literal: Unless he cultivates brilliance and fame, how can he repay this extraordinary favor?
translations.idiomatic: Unless he cultivates brilliance and fame, how can he repay this extraordinary favor?

sentences.zh: 匪崇徽烈，莫符天志。

translations.literal: Unless he elevates his fine virtue, how can he match Heaven's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Unless he elevates his fine virtue, how can he match Heaven's intent?

sentences.zh: 勉之又勉，光茲守器。

translations.literal: Strive and strive again—glorify your charge as guardian of the vessel of state!
translations.idiomatic: Strive and strive again—glorify your charge as guardian of the vessel of state!

sentences.zh: 下臣司箴，敢告近侍。

translations.literal: Your humble minister, charged with admonition, dares to address those who attend him closely.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble minister, charged with admonition, dares to address those who attend him closely.

sentences.zh: 太子表上其文，優詔賜帛四十匹，又令預撰《晉書》。

translations.literal: The crown prince submitted the text in a memorial. An edict of special favor granted forty bolts of silk, and [Yifu] was also ordered to take part in compiling the Book of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince submitted the text in a memorial. An edict of special favor granted forty bolts of silk, and Yifu was also ordered to take part in compiling the Book of Jin.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded to the throne, [Yifu] was transferred to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Yifu was transferred to Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，兼修國史，加弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he was additionally charged with compiling the national history and was made Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui he was additionally charged with compiling the national history and was made Academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 高宗將立武昭儀為皇后，義府嘗密申協贊，尋擢拜中書侍郎、同中書門下三品，監修國史，賜爵廣平縣男。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong was about to install Consort Wu Zhaoyi as empress, Yifu had secretly expressed his support. Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, given the same rank as the three chancellors, charged with supervising compilation of the national history, and granted the title Baron of Guangping County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong was about to install Consort Wu Zhaoyi as empress, Yifu had secretly expressed his support. Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat with chancellor rank, charged with supervising compilation of the national history, and granted the title Baron of Guangping County.

sentences.zh: 義府貌狀溫恭，與人語必嬉怡微笑，而褊忌陰賊。

translations.literal: Yifu in appearance was mild and courteous. When speaking with others he always smiled pleasantly, yet he was narrow-minded, jealous, and secretly malicious.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu looked mild and courteous. When he spoke with others he always smiled pleasantly, yet he was narrow-minded, jealous, and secretly malicious.

sentences.zh: 既處權要，欲人附己，微忤意者，輒加傾陷。

translations.literal: Once he held a position of power, he wanted others to attach themselves to him; whoever slightly displeased him, he would at once bring down and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held power, he wanted others to attach themselves to him; whoever slightly displeased him, he would at once bring down and ruin.

sentences.zh: 故時人言義府笑中有刀，又以其柔而害物，亦謂之「李貓。」

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time said that Yifu had a knife hidden in his smile, and because he was soft yet harmed others, they also called him "Li the Cat."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore people of the time said that Yifu had a knife hidden in his smile, and because he was soft yet harmed others, they also called him "Li the Cat."

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，以本官兼太子右庶子，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, in his original post he was additionally made Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent and advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing, retaining his original post, he was additionally made Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent and advanced in rank to marquis.

sentences.zh: 有洛州婦人淳于氏，坐奸繫於大理，義府聞其姿色，囑大理丞畢正義求為別宅婦，特為雪其罪。

translations.literal: There was a woman of Luozhou named Lady Chunyu, imprisoned at the Court of Judicial Review on a charge of adultery. Yifu heard of her beauty and instructed Vice Director Bi Zhengyi of the Court of Judicial Review to obtain her as a woman for his separate residence, and specially had her crime cleared.
translations.idiomatic: There was a woman of Luozhou named Lady Chunyu, imprisoned at the Court of Judicial Review on a charge of adultery. Yifu heard of her beauty and instructed Vice Director Bi Zhengyi of the Court of Judicial Review to obtain her as a concubine for his separate residence, and specially had her crime cleared.

sentences.zh: 卿段寶玄疑其故，遽以狀聞，詔令按其事，正義惶懼自縊而死。

translations.literal: Senior Director Duan Baoxuan suspected the reason and hurriedly reported the matter in a memorial. An edict ordered an investigation of the affair, and Zhengyi, in fear and panic, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Senior Director Duan Baoxuan suspected the reason and hurriedly reported the matter in a memorial. An edict ordered an investigation, and Zhengyi, in fear and panic, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 侍御史王義方廷奏義府犯狀，因言其初容貌為劉洎、馬周所幸，由此得進，言詞猥褻。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Wang Yifang memorialized in court Yifu's offenses, and further said that at first his appearance had been favored by Liu Ji and Ma Zhou, by which he had advanced; his language was obscene and lewd.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Wang Yifang memorialized in court on Yifu's offenses, and further said that at first his handsome appearance had been favored by Liu Ji and Ma Zhou, by which he had advanced; his language was obscene and lewd.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，出義方為萊州司戶，而不問義府奸濫之罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent Yifang out as registrar of Laizhou, but did not inquire into Yifu's crimes of adultery and abuse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and sent Yifang out as registrar of Laizhou, but did not inquire into Yifu's crimes of adultery and abuse.

sentences.zh: 義府云：「王御史妄相彈奏，得無愧乎？」

translations.literal: Yifu said: "Censor Wang recklessly memorialized against me—should he not feel ashamed?"
translations.idiomatic: Yifu said, "Censor Wang recklessly memorialized against me—should he not feel ashamed?"

sentences.zh: 義方對云：「仲尼為魯司寇七日，誅少正卯於兩觀之下；

translations.literal: Yifang replied: "Confucius, as Minister of Crime of Lu, within seven days executed Shaozheng Mao beneath the twin watchtowers;
translations.idiomatic: Yifang replied, "Confucius, as Minister of Crime of Lu, within seven days executed Shaozheng Mao beneath the twin watchtowers;

sentences.zh: 義方任御史旬有六日，不能去奸邪於雙闕之前，實以為愧。」

translations.literal: Yifang has served as censor for sixteen days and could not remove the wicked and corrupt before the twin palace gates—I truly feel ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: I have served as censor for sixteen days and could not remove the wicked and corrupt before the twin palace gates—I truly feel ashamed."

sentences.zh: 尋兼太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Soon [Yifu] was additionally made Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yifu was additionally made Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年，代崔敦禮為中書令，兼檢校御史大夫，監修國史、學士並如故。

translations.literal: In the second year [of Xianqing] he replaced Cui Dunli as Director of the Secretariat, additionally serving as acting Censor-in-Chief; his charge over compilation of the national history and his status as academician remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he replaced Cui Dunli as Director of the Secretariat, additionally serving as acting Censor-in-Chief; his charge over compilation of the national history and his status as academician remained as before.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子賓客，進封河間郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Mentor to the Heir Apparent and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made Mentor to the Heir Apparent and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Hejian Commandery.

sentences.zh: 三年，又追贈其父德晟為魏州刺史，諸子孩抱者並列清官，詔為造甲第，榮寵莫之能比。

translations.literal: In the third year his father Desheng was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Weizhou; all his sons, even those still in arms, were given posts in the pure offices. An edict ordered a grand mansion built for him—honor and favor none could match.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year his father Desheng was posthumously enfeoffed as prefect of Weizhou; all his sons, even those still in arms, were given posts in the pure offices. An edict ordered a grand mansion built for him—honor and favor none could match.

sentences.zh: 而義府貪冒無厭，與母、妻及諸子、女婿賣官鬻獄，其門如市。

translations.literal: Yet Yifu was greedy and insatiable. Together with his mother, wife, sons, and sons-in-law he sold offices and traded in judicial verdicts; his gate was like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yifu was greedy and insatiable. Together with his mother, wife, sons, and sons-in-law he sold offices and traded in judicial verdicts; his gate was like a market.

sentences.zh: 多引腹心，廣樹朋黨，傾動朝野。

translations.literal: He brought in many trusted intimates and widely planted factions, shaking court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in many trusted intimates and widely planted factions, shaking court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 初，杜正倫為中書侍郎，義府時任典儀，至是乃與正倫同為中書令。

translations.literal: Earlier, Du Zhenglun had been Vice Director of the Secretariat while Yifu had held the post of Ceremonial Officer; now the two of them served together as Directors of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Du Zhenglun had been Vice Director of the Secretariat while Yifu had held the post of Ceremonial Officer; now the two of them served together as Directors of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正倫每以先進自處，不下義府，而中書侍郎李友益密與正倫共圖議義府，更相伺察。

translations.literal: Zhenglun always placed himself as the senior man and would not defer to Yifu, while Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Youyi secretly joined Zhenglun in plotting against Yifu; they watched and investigated each other in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun always placed himself as the senior man and would not defer to Yifu, while Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Youyi secretly joined Zhenglun in plotting against Yifu; they watched and investigated each other in turn.

sentences.zh: 義府知而密令人封奏其事。

translations.literal: Yifu learned of this and secretly had someone submit a sealed memorial reporting the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu learned of this and secretly had someone submit a sealed memorial reporting the affair.

sentences.zh: 正倫與義府訟於上前，各有曲直。

translations.literal: Zhenglun and Yifu argued their case before the emperor; each had points in his favor and against.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun and Yifu argued their case before the emperor; each had points in his favor and against.

sentences.zh: 上以大臣不和，兩責之，左貶義府為普州刺史，正倫為橫州刺史，友益配流峰州。

translations.literal: Because the great ministers were not in harmony, the emperor rebuked them both and demoted Yifu to prefect of Puzhou and Zhenglun to prefect of Hengzhou; Youyi was sentenced to exile in Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because the great ministers were not in harmony, the emperor rebuked them both and demoted Yifu to prefect of Puzhou and Zhenglun to prefect of Hengzhou; Youyi was sentenced to exile in Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，復召義府兼吏部尚書、同中書門下三品，自余官封如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Yifu was recalled and additionally made Minister of the Civil Service with the same rank as the three chancellors; his other offices and enfeoffments remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Yifu was recalled and additionally made Minister of the Civil Service with chancellor rank; his other offices and enfeoffments remained as before.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，丁母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo he left office upon mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longshuo he left office upon mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 二年，起復為司列太常伯、同東西台三品。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled from mourning as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with the same rank as the three chancellors of the Eastern and Western Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled from mourning as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with chancellor rank in the Eastern and Western Offices.

sentences.zh: 義府尋請改葬其祖父，營墓於永康陵側。

translations.literal: Yifu soon requested to reinter his grandfather and built a tomb beside Yongkang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu soon requested to reinter his grandfather and built a tomb beside Yongkang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 三原令李孝節私課丁夫車牛，為其載土築墳，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: Magistrate Li Xiaojie of Sanyuan privately levied corvée laborers, carts, and oxen to haul earth and build the mound for him, working day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Li Xiaojie of Sanyuan privately levied corvée laborers, carts, and oxen to haul earth and build the mound for him, working day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 於是高陵、櫟陽、富平、雲陽、華原、同官、涇陽等七縣，以孝節之故，懼不得已，悉課丁車赴役。

translations.literal: Thereupon the seven counties of Gaoling, Liyang, Fuping, Yunyang, Huayuan, Tongguan, and Jingyang, because of Xiaojie, fearing they had no choice, all levied corvée laborers and carts to go to the work.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the seven counties of Gaoling, Liyang, Fuping, Yunyang, Huayuan, Tongguan, and Jingyang, fearing they had no choice because of Xiaojie, all levied corvée laborers and carts to go to the work.

sentences.zh: 高陵令張敬業恭勤怯懦，不堪其勞，死於作所。

translations.literal: Magistrate Zhang Jingye of Gaoling, though respectful and diligent, was timid and weak and could not endure the labor; he died at the work site.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Zhang Jingye of Gaoling, though respectful and diligent, was timid and weak and could not endure the labor; he died at the work site.

sentences.zh: 王公已下，爭致贈遺，其羽儀、導從、轜輶、器服，並窮極奢侈。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes downward, all vied to send gifts. The ceremonial guards, escorts, carriages, and accoutrements were all pushed to the utmost extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes downward, all vied to send gifts. The ceremonial guards, escorts, carriages, and accoutrements were all pushed to the utmost extravagance.

sentences.zh: 又會葬車馬祖奠供帳，自灞橋屬於三原，七十里間，相繼不絕。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the joint burial the funeral carriages, offerings at the roadside, and provision tents stretched from Baa Bridge to Sanyuan—a distance of seventy li—unbroken in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at the joint burial the funeral carriages, roadside offerings, and provision tents stretched from Ba Bridge to Sanyuan—a distance of seventy li—unbroken in succession.

sentences.zh: 武德已來，王公葬送之盛，未始有也。

translations.literal: Since Wude, the splendor of princely and ducal funerals had never been seen before.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wude era, the splendor of princely and ducal funerals had never been seen before.

sentences.zh: 義府本無藻鑑才，怙武後之勢，專以賣官為事。

translations.literal: Yifu originally had no talent for discerning men. Relying on Empress Wu's power, he devoted himself solely to selling offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu originally had no talent for discerning men. Relying on Empress Wu's power, he devoted himself solely to selling offices.

sentences.zh: 銓序失次，人多怨讟。

translations.literal: The order of appointments was disrupted and many people complained and cursed.
translations.idiomatic: The order of appointments was disrupted and many people complained and cursed.

sentences.zh: 時殷王初出閣，又以義府兼王府長史。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Yin had just left the palace precinct, and Yifu was additionally made chief administrator of the princely household.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Yin had just left the palace precinct, and Yifu was additionally made chief administrator of the princely household.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷右相，殷王府長史仍知選事並如故。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Right Chancellor; his post as chief administrator of the princely household and his charge over appointments remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Right Chancellor; his post as chief administrator of the princely household and his charge over appointments remained as before.

sentences.zh: 義府入則諂言自媚，出則肆其奸宄，百僚畏之，無敢言其過者。

translations.literal: Yifu, when inside, flattered with fawning words; when outside, he gave free rein to his wickedness. The hundred officials feared him, and none dared speak of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu, when inside, flattered with fawning words; when outside, he gave free rein to his wickedness. The hundred officials feared him, and none dared speak of his faults.

sentences.zh: 帝頗知其罪失，從容誡義府云：「聞卿兒子、女婿皆不謹慎，多作罪過，我亦為卿掩覆，未即公言，卿可誡勖，勿令如此。」

translations.literal: The emperor was quite aware of his faults and offenses. He calmly admonished Yifu, saying: "I hear that your sons and sons-in-law are all careless and commit many offenses. I have also covered for you and have not spoken of it publicly. You should warn and encourage them—do not let them go on this way."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was quite aware of his faults and offenses. He calmly admonished Yifu, saying, "I hear that your sons and sons-in-law are all careless and commit many offenses. I have also covered for you and have not spoken of it publicly. You should warn and encourage them—do not let them go on this way."

sentences.zh: 義府勃然變色，腮頸俱起，徐曰：「誰向陛下道此？」

translations.literal: Yifu suddenly changed color in anger; his cheeks and neck both flushed. He said slowly: "Who told Your Majesty this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yifu suddenly flushed with anger; his cheeks and neck both reddened. He said slowly, "Who told Your Majesty this?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「但我言如是，何須問我所從得耶！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "But I speak thus—why must you ask where I heard it from!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "But I speak thus—why must you ask where I heard it from!"

sentences.zh: 義府睆然，殊不引咎，緩步而去。

translations.literal: Yifu stared blankly, showed no sign of accepting blame, and walked away at an unhurried pace.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu stared blankly, showed no sign of accepting blame, and walked away at an unhurried pace.

sentences.zh: 上亦優容之。

translations.literal: The emperor also treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also treated him with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 初，五禮儀注，自前代相沿，吉凶畢舉。

translations.literal: Earlier, the ceremonial regulations for the Five Rites, handed down from former ages, included both auspicious and inauspicious rites in full.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the ceremonial regulations for the Five Rites, handed down from former ages, included both auspicious and inauspicious rites in full.

sentences.zh: 太常博士蕭楚材、孔志約以皇室凶禮為預備凶事，非臣子所宜言之。

translations.literal: Academicians Xiao Chucai and Kong Zhiyue of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices held that the imperial mourning rites, as preparations for inauspicious events, were not what subjects should speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians Xiao Chucai and Kong Zhiyue of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices held that the imperial mourning rites, as preparations for inauspicious events, were not what subjects should speak of.

sentences.zh: 義府深然之。

translations.literal: Yifu deeply agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu deeply agreed with this.

sentences.zh: 於是悉刪而焚焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had them all deleted and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he had them all deleted and burned.

sentences.zh: 義府既貴之後，又自言本出趙郡，始與諸李敘昭穆，而無賴之徒苟合，藉其權勢，拜伏為兄叔者甚眾。

translations.literal: After Yifu had risen to high rank, he also declared that his family originally came from Zhao Commandery and began to arrange senior and junior relations with various members of the Li clan. Rascals who attached themselves to him, relying on his power, were many who bowed and called him elder brother or uncle.
translations.idiomatic: After Yifu had risen to high rank, he also declared that his family originally came from Zhao Commandery and began to arrange senior and junior relations with various members of the Li clan. Many rascals who attached themselves to him, relying on his power, bowed and called him elder brother or uncle.

sentences.zh: 給事中李崇德初亦與同譜敘昭穆，及義府出為普州刺史，遂即除削。

translations.literal: Attendant Li Chongde at first also joined with him in arranging the clan genealogy and seniority, but when Yifu was sent out as Prefect of Puzhou, he was at once struck from the roll.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Li Chongde had at first also joined him in arranging their clan genealogy, but when Yifu was demoted to Prefect of Puzhou, Chongde was immediately struck from the roll.

sentences.zh: 義府聞而銜之，及重為宰相，乃令人誣構其罪，竟下獄自殺。

translations.literal: Yifu heard of this and bore a grudge; when he again became chief minister, he had someone fabricate charges against him, and in the end he was thrown into prison and committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu heard of this and bore a grudge. When he again became chief minister, he had charges fabricated against Chongde, who was thrown into prison and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 初，貞觀中，太宗命吏部尚書高士廉、御史大夫韋挺、中書侍郎岑文本、禮部侍郎令狐德棻等及四方士大夫諳練門閥者修《氏族志》，勒成百卷，升降去取，時稱允當，頒下諸州，藏為永式。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Zhenguan era, the Taizong Emperor ordered Minister of Personnel Gao Shilian, Censor-in-Chief Wei Ting, Secretariat Vice Director Cen Wenti, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others, together with gentlemen from all quarters versed in distinguished clans, to compile the Genealogies of Clans. The work was completed in a hundred scrolls; promotions and demotions in rank were at the time called fair and appropriate. It was distributed to all prefectures and preserved as a permanent standard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Zhenguan era, Emperor Taizong ordered Gao Shilian, Wei Ting, Cen Wenti, Linghu Defen, and other officials, together with scholars versed in distinguished clans from across the realm, to compile the Genealogies of Clans. The work ran to a hundred scrolls, and its rankings were widely judged fair. It was distributed to all prefectures and preserved as a permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 義府恥其家代無名，乃奏改此書，專委禮部郎中孔志約、著作郎楊仁卿、太子洗馬史玄道、太常丞呂才重修。

translations.literal: Yifu was ashamed that his family for generations had been without renown and therefore memorialized to revise this book, specially entrusting Section Director of Rites Kong Zhiyue, Compiler Yang Renqing, Crown Prince's Libationer Shi Xuandao, and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lü Cai to revise it anew.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed that his family had for generations lacked renown, Yifu memorialized to revise the work and entrusted Kong Zhiyue, Yang Renqing, Shi Xuandao, and Lü Cai with a full revision.

sentences.zh: 志約等遂立格云：「皇朝得五品官者，皆升士流。」

translations.literal: Zhiyue and the others thereupon established a rule saying: "In our dynasty, all who obtain office of the fifth rank are to be raised into the gentry stream."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyue and the others then established a rule: "In our dynasty, all who obtain office of the fifth rank are to be entered among the gentry."

sentences.zh: 於是兵卒以軍功致五品者，盡入書限，更名為《姓氏錄》。

translations.literal: Thereupon soldiers and commoners who through military merit reached the fifth rank all entered the limits of the book, and it was renamed the Register of Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon soldiers who through military merit reached the fifth rank were all entered in the register, which was renamed the Register of Surnames.

sentences.zh: 由是搢紳士大夫多恥被甄敘，皆號此書為「勳格」。

translations.literal: Because of this, many gentry and scholar-officials were ashamed to be entered in the selection and all called this book the "Merit Register."
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, many gentry and scholar-officials were ashamed to be listed in it and called the book the "Merit Register."

sentences.zh: 義府仍奏收天下《氏族志》本焚之。

translations.literal: Yifu still memorialized to collect all copies of the Genealogies of Clans throughout the realm and burn them.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu also memorialized to collect all copies of the Genealogies of Clans throughout the realm and burn them.

sentences.zh: 關東魏、齊舊姓，雖皆淪替，猶相矜尚，自為婚姻。

translations.literal: The old surnames of Wei and Qi east of the Pass, though all had fallen from power, still prided themselves on one another and formed marriages among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The old families of Wei and Qi east of the Pass, though fallen from power, still prided themselves on their standing and married only among themselves.

sentences.zh: 義府為子求婚不得，乃奏隴西李等七家，不得相與為婚。

translations.literal: When Yifu could not obtain a marriage for his son, he memorialized that the seven families including the Li of Longxi must not intermarry with one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Yifu failed to secure a marriage for his son, he memorialized that the seven great families, including the Li of Longxi, must not intermarry with one another.

sentences.zh: 陰陽占候人杜元紀為義府望氣，雲「所居宅有獄氣，發積錢二千萬乃可厭勝。」

translations.literal: The yin-yang diviner Du Yuanji practiced qi observation for Yifu and said: "The residence you dwell in has the qi of prison; only by spending twenty million in accumulated cash can it be overcome."
translations.idiomatic: The yin-yang diviner Du Yuanji read the qi of Yifu's residence and said, "Your house bears the qi of imprisonment; only by spending twenty million cash from your hoard can the omen be overcome."

sentences.zh: 義府信之，聚斂更急切。

translations.literal: Yifu believed him and exacted levies all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu believed him and extorted wealth all the more ruthlessly.

sentences.zh: 義府居母服，有制朔望給哭假，義府輒微服與元紀凌晨共出城東，登古冢候望，哀禮都廢。

translations.literal: While Yifu was in mourning for his mother, regulations provided leave for weeping on the first and fifteenth of the month, yet Yifu would put on ordinary dress and go out with Yuanji at dawn to the east of the city, climb an ancient tomb, and observe the omens, utterly abandoning mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning for his mother, Yifu was granted leave to weep on the first and fifteenth of each month, yet he would don ordinary dress and go out with Yuanji at dawn to the east of the city, climb an ancient tomb to observe the omens, and utterly abandon mourning propriety.

sentences.zh: 由是人皆言其窺覘災眚，陰懷異圖。

translations.literal: Because of this everyone said he was watching for calamities and secretly harbored irregular designs.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this everyone said he was watching for omens of disaster and secretly harbored treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 義府又遣其子右司議郎津，召長孫無忌之孫延，謂曰：「相為得一官，數日詔書當出。」

translations.literal: Yifu also sent his son Jin, Right Secretariat Discussant, to summon Yan, grandson of Zhangsun Wuji, and said to him: "I will get you an office; in a few days the edict will issue."
translations.idiomatic: Yifu also sent his son Jin, a Right Secretariat Discussant, to summon Yan, grandson of Zhangsun Wuji, and told him, "I will secure you an office; the edict will issue in a few days."

sentences.zh: 居五日，果授延司津監，乃取延錢七百貫。

translations.literal: After five days Yan was indeed appointed Director of the Ferry Office, and he then took from Yan seven hundred strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later Yan was indeed appointed Director of the Ferry Office, and Jin then took seven hundred strings of cash from him.

sentences.zh: 於是右金吾倉曹參軍楊行穎表言義府罪狀，制下司刑太常伯劉祥道與侍御詳刑對推其事，仍令司空李勣監焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Right Golden Guards Warehouse Section Military Adjutant Yang Xingying memorialized stating Yifu's crimes. An edict ordered Minister of Punishments Liu Xiangdao and the Attending Censor for Detailed Punishment jointly to investigate the matter, with Sikong Li Ji still ordered to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yang Xingying, a military adjutant of the Right Golden Guards, memorialized detailing Yifu's crimes. An edict ordered Liu Xiangdao and the attending censor for detailed punishment to investigate jointly, with Sikong Li Ji supervising.

sentences.zh: 按皆有實，乃下制曰：「右相、行殷王府長史、河間郡公李義府，洩禁中之語，鬻寵授之朝恩；
