translations.literal: The investigation found everything substantiated, and an edict was issued saying: "Right Chancellor, Acting Chief Administrator of the Prince of Yin's household, Duke of Hejian Commandery Li Yifu leaked words from within the forbidden precincts and sold favor to trade for court grace;
translations.idiomatic: The investigation substantiated every charge, and an edict declared: "Right Chancellor, Acting Chief Administrator of the Prince of Yin's household, Duke of Hejian Commandery Li Yifu leaked words from within the forbidden precincts and sold imperial favor for personal gain;

sentences.zh: 交占候之人，輕朔望之哀禮。

translations.literal: he associated with diviners of omens and treated lightly the mourning rites of the first and fifteenth;
translations.idiomatic: he consorted with diviners and treated lightly the mourning rites due on the first and fifteenth of the month;

sentences.zh: 蓄邪黷貨，實玷衣冠；

translations.literal: he hoarded wickedness and amassed corrupt wealth, truly staining the robes of office;
translations.idiomatic: he hoarded wickedness and amassed corrupt wealth, truly staining the dignity of office;

sentences.zh: 稔惡嫉賢，載虧政道。

translations.literal: his evil ripened and he envied the worthy, greatly harming the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: his wickedness ripened and he envied the worthy, greatly harming the conduct of government.

sentences.zh: 特以任使多年，未忍便加重罰，宜從遐棄，以肅朝倫。

translations.literal: Specially because he has been employed for many years, We cannot bear at once to impose heavy punishment; he should be cast off to a distant place to rectify court order.
translations.idiomatic: Because he has served for many years, We cannot bear to impose the heaviest punishment at once; he should be cast off to a distant place to restore order at court.

sentences.zh: 可除名長流巂州。

translations.literal: His name may be struck and he may be exiled for life to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His name is struck from the rolls and he is exiled for life to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 其子太子右司議郎津，專恃權門，罕懷忌憚，姦淫是務，賄賂無厭，交遊非所，潛報機密，亦宜明罰，屏跡荒裔。

translations.literal: His son Jin, Right Secretariat Discussant of the Heir Apparent, relied solely on the gate of power, rarely felt restraint, made lewdness his business, was insatiable in bribes, associated with improper persons, and secretly reported confidential matters. He too should receive clear punishment and be banished to the wild borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin, a Right Secretariat Discussant of the Heir Apparent, relied solely on his father's power, rarely showed restraint, devoted himself to lewdness, was insatiable in bribes, consorted with improper persons, and secretly reported confidential matters. He too should be clearly punished and banished to the wild borderlands.

sentences.zh: 可除名長流振州。」

translations.literal: His name may be struck and he may be exiled for life to Zhenzhou."
translations.idiomatic: His name is struck from the rolls and he is exiled for life to Zhenzhou."

sentences.zh: 義府次子率府長史洽、千牛備身洋、子婿少府主簿柳元貞等，皆憑恃受贓，併除名長流延州。

translations.literal: Yifu's second son Qia, Chief Secretary of the Crown Prince's Guard; Yang, Imperial Guard Attendant; and his son-in-law Liu Yuanzhen, Secretary of the Palace Storehouse—all relied on his power to accept bribes and were likewise struck from the rolls and exiled for life to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu's second son Qia, his son Yang, and his son-in-law Liu Yuanzhen all relied on his power to accept bribes and were likewise struck from the rolls and exiled for life to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝野莫不稱慶，時人為之語曰：「今日巨唐年，還誅四凶族。」

translations.literal: Court and common people alike rejoiced without exception. People of the time made a saying: "In this great Tang year, the four wicked clans are at last punished."
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike rejoiced. People of the time said, "In this great Tang year, the four wicked clans are at last punished."

sentences.zh: 四凶者，謂洽及柳元貞等四人也。

translations.literal: The four wicked ones meant Qia and Liu Yuanzhen and four others.
translations.idiomatic: The four wicked ones referred to Qia, Liu Yuanzhen, and the others—four men in all.

sentences.zh: 或作《河間道行軍元帥劉祥道破銅山大賊李義府露布》，榜之通衢。

translations.literal: Someone composed a Field Dispatch on Campaign Marshal Liu Xiangdao of the Hejian Circuit defeating the great bandit Li Yifu of Copper Mountain and posted it in the public thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: Someone composed a field dispatch entitled "Campaign Marshal Liu Xiangdao of the Hejian Circuit Defeats the Great Bandit Li Yifu of Copper Mountain" and posted it in the public streets.

sentences.zh: 義府先多取人奴婢，及敗，一時奔散，各歸其家。

translations.literal: Yifu had earlier taken many people's slaves and maidservants; when he fell, they all at once scattered and each returned to his own home.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu had earlier seized many people's slaves and servants; when he fell, they all scattered at once and each returned home.

sentences.zh: 《露布》稱「混奴婢而亂放，各識家而競入」者，謂此也。

translations.literal: The dispatch's phrase "mixing slaves and maidservants and releasing them in disorder, each recognizing his home and rushing to enter" referred to this.
translations.idiomatic: The dispatch's line about "mixing slaves and servants and releasing them in disorder, each recognizing his home and rushing to enter" referred to this.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年，大赦，長流人不許還，義府憂憤發疾卒，年五十餘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng there was a general amnesty, but those exiled for life were not permitted to return. Yifu, aggrieved and indignant, fell ill and died, aged somewhat over fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In 666 a general amnesty was proclaimed, but those exiled for life were not permitted to return. Yifu, aggrieved and indignant, fell ill and died at somewhat over fifty years of age.

sentences.zh: 文集三十捲，傳於代；

translations.literal: His collected writings were thirty scrolls, transmitted to the age;
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to thirty scrolls and were transmitted to later ages;

sentences.zh: 又著《宦遊記》二十捲，尋亡失。

translations.literal: he also authored Records of Official Travel in twenty scrolls, which soon were lost.
translations.idiomatic: he also wrote Records of Official Travel in twenty scrolls, which were soon lost.

sentences.zh: 自義府流放後，朝士常憂懼，恐其復來，及聞其死，於是始安。

translations.literal: From the time Yifu was exiled, court gentlemen were constantly anxious and fearful lest he return; when they heard of his death, they were at last at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After Yifu was exiled, court officials lived in constant fear that he might return; when they heard of his death, they were at last at ease.

sentences.zh: 上元元年，大赦，義府妻子得還洛陽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan there was a general amnesty, and Yifu's wife and children were permitted to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 674 a general amnesty was proclaimed, and Yifu's wife and children were permitted to return to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 如意元年，則天以義府與許敬宗、御史大夫崔義玄、中書舍人王德儉、大理正侯善業、大理丞袁公瑜等六人，在永徽中有翊贊之功，追贈義府揚州大都督，義玄益州大都督，德儉魏州刺史，公瑜江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ruyi, Zetian, because Yifu together with Xu Jingzong, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yixuan, Palace Secretariat Drafter Wang Dejian, Senior Corrector of the Court of Judicial Review Hou Shanye, and Corrector of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Gongyu—six men who during Yonghui had rendered meritorious support—posthumously enfeoffed Yifu as Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, Yixuan as Area Commander-in-Chief of Yizhou, Dejian as Prefect of Weizhou, and Gongyu as Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 692 Empress Zetian, because Yifu together with Xu Jingzong, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yixuan, Palace Secretariat Drafter Wang Dejian, Senior Corrector of the Court of Judicial Review Hou Shanye, and Corrector of the Court of Judicial Review Yuan Gongyu—the six men who during the Yonghui era had rendered meritorious support—posthumously enfeoffed Yifu as Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou, Yixuan as Area Commander-in-Chief of Yizhou, Dejian as Prefect of Weizhou, and Gongyu as Prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 長安元年，又賜義府子左千牛衛將軍湛及敬宗諸子實封各三百戶，義玄子司賓卿基、德儉子殿中監璇實封各二百五十戶，善業子太子右庶子知一、公瑜子殿中丞忠臣實封各二百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chang'an, she furthermore granted Zhan, General of the Left Qianniu Guard and son of Yifu, and the various sons of Jingzong each three hundred households of enfeoffment in actuality; Ji, Director of Palace Receptions and son of Yixuan, and Xuan, Director of the Palace Domestic Service and son of Dejian, each two hundred fifty households; Zhiyi, Right Subdirector of the Crown Prince's household and son of Shanye, and Zhongchen, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace and son of Gongyu, each two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In 701 she furthermore granted Yifu's son Zhan, General of the Left Qianniu Guard, and the various sons of Jingzong each three hundred households of actual enfeoffment; Yixuan's son Ji, Director of Palace Receptions, and Dejian's son Xuan, Director of the Palace Domestic Service, each two hundred fifty households; and Shanye's son Zhiyi, Right Subdirector of the Crown Prince's household, and Gongyu's son Zhongchen, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace, each two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，景雲元年，並停義府等六家實封。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, in the first year of Jingyun, the actual enfeoffments of the six families including Yifu were all suspended.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, in 710 the actual enfeoffments of the six families including Yifu's were all suspended.

sentences.zh: 少子湛

translations.literal: The youngest son Zhan
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son, Zhan

sentences.zh: 義府少子湛，年六歲時，以父貴授周王文學。

translations.literal: Zhan, Yifu's youngest son, at the age of six because of his father's eminence was appointed Literary Scholar of the Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan, Yifu's youngest son, was at the age of six appointed Literary Scholar of the Prince of Zhou because of his father's eminence.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，累遷右散騎常侍，襲封河間郡公。

translations.literal: Early in the Shenlong era he was promoted in succession to Right Regular Attendant and inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he rose to Right Regular Attendant and inherited the title Duke of Hejian Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時鳳閣侍郎張柬之將誅張易之兄弟，遂引湛為左羽林將軍，令與敬暉等啟請皇太子，備陳將誅易之兄弟意，太子許之。

translations.literal: At that time Phoenix Pavilion Vice Director Zhang Jianzhi was about to execute the Zhang Yizhi brothers and therefore brought in Zhan as General of the Left Feathered Forest, ordering him together with Jing Hui and others to petition the crown prince, fully stating the plan to execute the Zhang brothers. The crown prince consented.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jianzhi, Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion, planned to execute the Zhang Yizhi brothers, he appointed Zhan General of the Left Feathered Forest and ordered him, together with Jing Hui and others, to petition the crown prince and explain the plan in full. The crown prince consented.

sentences.zh: 及兵發，湛與右羽林大將軍李多祚等詣東宮迎皇太子，拒而不時出，湛進啟曰：「逆豎反道亂常，將圖不軌，宗社危敗，實在須臾。

translations.literal: When the troops set out, Zhan together with Right Feathered Forest General-in-Chief Li Duozuo and others went to the Eastern Palace to welcome the crown prince, who refused and would not come out in good time. Zhan advanced and petitioned: "The rebellious villains violate the Way and disorder the norms, plotting irregular designs; the altars of state are in peril of ruin—truly it is a matter of moments.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops set out, Zhan and Li Duozuo, General-in-Chief of the Right Feathered Forest, went to the Eastern Palace to bring out the crown prince, who refused to come out promptly. Zhan stepped forward and said, "These rebels violate the Way and plot treason; the altars of state stand on the brink of ruin—this is a matter of moments.

sentences.zh: 湛等諸將與南衙執事剋期誅翦，伏願殿下暫至玄武門，以副眾望。」

translations.literal: Zhan and the other generals together with the officials of the Southern Yamen have set a date to cut down and destroy them. We humbly beg Your Highness for the moment to come to the Xuanwu Gate to fulfill the people's hope."
translations.idiomatic: We generals, together with the officials of the Southern Yamen, have set a date to strike them down. We humbly beg Your Highness to come at once to the Xuanwu Gate and fulfill the people's hope."

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「凶豎悖亂，誠合誅夷，然聖躬不豫，慮有驚動。

translations.literal: The crown prince said: "The wicked villains are rebellious and disorderly and truly ought to be executed, yet the sacred person is unwell and I fear there may be alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said, "These wicked men are rebellious and deserve execution, yet the sacred person is unwell and I fear there may be alarm.

sentences.zh: 公等且止，以俟後圖。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen stop for now and wait for a later plan."
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen must stop for now and wait for a later opportunity."

sentences.zh: 湛曰：「諸將棄家族，共宰相同心戮力，匡輔社稷，殿下奈何不哀其懇誠而欲陷之鼎鑊？

translations.literal: Zhan said: "The generals have abandoned their families and together with the chief minister exert their strength with one heart to support the altars of state. How can Your Highness fail to pity their earnest sincerity and instead wish to cast them into the cauldron?
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said, "These generals have abandoned their families and, together with the chief minister, exert all their strength to save the realm. How can Your Highness fail to pity their earnest devotion and instead wish to cast them into the cauldron?

sentences.zh: 湛等微命，雖不足惜，殿下速出自止遏。」

translations.literal: Zhan and the others' slight lives, though not worth cherishing—Your Highness must quickly come out yourself to stop and restrain them."
translations.idiomatic: Our slight lives are not worth cherishing, but Your Highness must come out at once to restrain the situation."

sentences.zh: 太子乃馳馬就路。

translations.literal: The crown prince thereupon spurred his horse and took the road.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince thereupon spurred his horse and set out.

sentences.zh: 湛從至玄武門，斬關而入，率所部兵直至則天所寢長生殿，環繞侍衛。

translations.literal: Zhan followed to the Xuanwu Gate, cut through the barrier and entered, and led the troops under his command straight to the Everlasting Life Hall where Zetian slept, surrounding it in guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan followed to the Xuanwu Gate, broke through the barrier, and led his troops straight to the Everlasting Life Hall where Empress Zetian lay, surrounding it with guards.

sentences.zh: 因奏：「臣等奉令誅逆賊易之、昌宗，恐有漏洩，遂不獲預奏，輒陳兵禁掖，是臣等死罪。」

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized: "Your servants received orders to execute the traitors Yizhi and Changzong. Fearing leakage, we could not obtain prior memorialization and rashly presented troops in the forbidden inner quarters—this is your servants' crime deserving death."
translations.idiomatic: He reported, "We received orders to execute the traitors Yizhi and Changzong. Fearing a leak, we could not report in advance and rashly brought troops into the forbidden inner quarters—this is our crime deserving death."

sentences.zh: 則天謂湛曰：「卿亦是誅易之軍將耶？

translations.literal: Zetian said to Zhan: "Are you also a general in the army that executes Yizhi?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian said to Zhan, "Are you also one of the generals sent to execute Yizhi?

sentences.zh: 我於汝父子恩不少，何至是也！」

translations.literal: I have shown your father and son no small favor—how could it come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: I have shown your father and you no small favor—how could it come to this!"

sentences.zh: 則天移就上陽宮，因留湛宿衛。

translations.literal: Zetian was moved to the Shangyang Palace, and Zhan was left behind to guard overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian was moved to the Shangyang Palace, and Zhan was left behind to stand guard.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，拜右羽林大將軍，進封趙國公，加實封通前滿五百戶。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, Zhan was appointed General of the Right Feathered Forest, advanced to Duke of Zhao, and given enfeoffment in actual households reaching five hundred together with what he had before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, Zhan was appointed General of the Right Feathered Forest, ennobled as Duke of Zhao, and granted enfeoffment in actual households totaling five hundred.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復授左散騎常侍，累轉左領軍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly he was again appointed Left Regular Attendant and was promoted in succession to General-in-Chief of the Left Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Left Regular Attendant and later rose to General-in-Chief of the Left Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 開元初卒。

translations.literal: Early in the Kaiyuan era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 崔義玄別有傳。

translations.literal: Cui Yixuan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yixuan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰

translations.literal: The historian says:
translations.idiomatic: The historian says:

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：許高陽武德之際，已為文皇入館之賓，垂三十年，位不過列曹尹；

translations.literal: The historian says: Xu of Gaoyang in the Wude era was already a guest whom the Literary Emperor brought into his household. For nearly thirty years his rank did not exceed a departmental director;
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Xu of Gaoyang in the Wude era was already a guest whom Emperor Taizong brought into his household. For nearly thirty years his rank never rose above a departmental director;

sentences.zh: 而馬周、劉洎起羈旅徒步，六七年間，皆登宰執。

translations.literal: yet Ma Zhou and Liu Ji, rising from travelers on foot in exile, within six or seven years all reached chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: yet Ma Zhou and Liu Ji, who began as humble travelers, within six or seven years both reached the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 考其行實，則高陽之文學宏奧，周、洎無以過之，然而太宗任遇相殊者，良以高陽才優而行薄故也。

translations.literal: Examining their conduct and achievements, Gaoyang's literary learning was grand and profound, which Zhou and Ji could not surpass; yet the reason the Taizong Emperor's appointment and favor differed so was truly because Gaoyang's talent was superior but his conduct was thin.
translations.idiomatic: Examining their conduct and achievements, Gaoyang's literary learning was grand and profound, which Zhou and Ji could not surpass; yet the reason Emperor Taizong favored them so differently was truly that Gaoyang's talent was superior but his conduct was wanting.

sentences.zh: 及屬嗣君沖暗，嬖妾奸邪，阿附豺狼，窺圖權軸，人之凶險，一至於斯。

translations.literal: When it fell to a successor ruler who was dull and dim, with favored concubines and wicked ministers, he attached himself to wolves, schemed for the pivot of power—the viciousness of a man reaches even to this.
translations.idiomatic: When the succession fell to a dull and dim ruler, with favored concubines and wicked ministers, he attached himself to wolves and schemed for the pivot of power—the viciousness of a man can reach even to this.

sentences.zh: 仲尼所謂「雖有周公之才，不足觀也。」

translations.literal: What Confucius called "though he has the talent of the Duke of Zhou, he is not worth observing."
translations.idiomatic: What Confucius called "though he has the talent of the Duke of Zhou, he is not worth observing."

sentences.zh: 義府才思精密，所謂「猩猩能言」，鄙哉！

translations.literal: Yifu's literary thought was precise and subtle—what is called "the orangutan can speak"—how base!
translations.idiomatic: Yifu's literary thought was precise and subtle—what people call "the orangutan can speak"—how base!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：貞觀文士，高陽、河間。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Literary gentlemen of the Zhenguan era—Gaoyang and Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Literary gentlemen of the Zhenguan era—Gaoyang and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 圖形學館，染翰書山。

translations.literal: Their images were painted in the academic halls; they stained their brushes on the mountain of books.
translations.idiomatic: Their images were painted in the academic halls; they stained their brushes on the mountain of books.

sentences.zh: 進身以筆，得位由奸。

translations.literal: They advanced through the brush and obtained position through wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced through the brush and obtained position through wickedness.

sentences.zh: 為虎傅翼，即又胡顏。

translations.literal: Giving wings to a tiger—how then could they show their faces?
translations.idiomatic: Giving wings to a tiger—how then could they show their faces?
